READ THIS FIRST


WHY YOU DON'T HAVE ENOUGH
LEADS
There are only two reasons, and every marketing problem you have rolls up into one of
them:


    THE TWO TRUTHS

    1. People don't know you exist.

    2. The very few who do know you haven't been given enough reason to believe
    you.


That's the whole game. Everything in this roadmap either makes more people know about you or
gives them more reasons to believe you. And I mean it when I say people don't know you exist.
During one of our book launches we had spent four to five million dollars on advertising, and when I
stopped people on the street, 19 out of 20 of my own followers had no idea a book was coming.
People who already followed me. After millions in ads.

Internalize that. The market is unbelievably large and your attempts at being known are small and
short-lived. When you feel like you've saturated your market, you've almost always just saturated the
tiny segment your current message speaks to.


THE WHOLE BUSINESS, IN ONE BOX

A business is a box that turns attention into money. Attention goes in one side, your money model
does its work in the middle, and money comes out the other side. Once the box works, there's
exactly one question that matters: why aren't you shoving more attention into it?

This roadmap exists because the answer to that question changes as you grow. What blocks the
box at $10K a month is different from what blocks it at $10M a year. Six stages, six different blocks, six
different jobs.


    "All growth is constrained by irrelevance."
    ALEX HORMOZI

BEFORE STAGE ONE


FOUR RULES THAT APPLY AT EVERY
STAGE
RULE 1 — VOLUME NEGATES LUCK

Quantity has a quality of its own. Advertising is a game of massive assault. The businesses that look
"lucky" are doing 30 times your advertising activity, which is why they get 30 times your sales. When
your results feel volatile, you're not unlucky. You're just not doing enough for the numbers to stabilize.


RULE 2 — STATE THE FACTS AND TELL THE TRUTH

This is the number one marketing rule at Acquisition.com. And here's the magic: if the facts aren't
compelling, you don't warp the facts. You warp reality. Go get the 20,000 five-star reviews. Go create
the result worth talking about. Then marketing becomes stating what's true.


RULE 3 — NOBODY BELIEVES YOU

Proof, despite all the praise it gets, is still underrated. Say what only you can say. Show what only you
can show. If I could stand next to 20,000 five-star reviews, I wouldn't need to say much at all. Every
stage of this roadmap assumes you keep collecting proof, forever.


RULE 4 — MARKETING ALWAYS WORKS. IT'S A MATTER OF EFFICIENCY.

"Meta ads don't work for me" is not a real sentence. The real sentence is "I don't know how to make
Meta ads efficient enough for my business yet." The first version is out of your control. The second
one is a to-do list. Debug one step at a time: are people clicking? Are clickers opting in? Are opt-ins
booking? Are bookings showing? Fix the one step in front of you.


    "Tell people what you have and make sure they understand that it's for
    them."
    ALEX HORMOZI


One warning before you dive in: the idiot and the genius agree on the line above. The midwit obsesses over ad length,
button colors, and posting times. When in doubt, assume your customer has no idea who you are, is in a rush, and reads at
a third-grade level. Deletion will often beat explanation.

 QUESTION                                                IF THE ANSWER IS NO


 1. Could you handle more customers right now?           Leads are not your problem. Go fix delivery and capacity first.

 spend more, post more, reach out more today?)           go do more. Spend more. Post more. Call more. You don't have a
                                                         strategy problem, you have a volume problem.

 much vs. your industry average?                         the problem isn't marketing. It's what a customer is worth to you.

 4. Or do too few leads convert?                         That's a sales problem. Benchmark by mechanism: in-person
                                                         with a salesperson should close around 30%, webinars around 10
                                                         to 15%. Fix the mechanism before buying more leads.

THE METHOD


THE CORE THREE
Almost every business on earth acquires customers through some combination of
three methods. There is no fourth secret one.


  Ads                                      Content                             Outreach
  PAY PLATFORMS TO PUT YOUR                PUBLISH THINGS PEOPLE WANT TO       CONTACT PEOPLE DIRECTLY, ONE
  MESSAGE IN FRONT OF STRANGERS.           WATCH AND READ. SLOWEST TO          TO ONE. STARTS TODAY, COSTS
  FASTEST TO SCALE, COSTS CASH.            START, COMPOUNDS FOREVER.           LABOR.


HOW TO PICK YOURS

There are many ways up the mountain, and the paths mostly work. So don't pick by ideology, pick by
risk-adjusted return on the skills and resources you already have. Done ads before? Do more, better
ads. Built an audience before? More, better content. Good on the phone? More, better outreach.
Replace right-versus-wrong thinking with likelihoods and returns.


THE FIX ORDER INSIDE ANY CHANNEL

When a channel underperforms, fix things in this order, because this is the order of leverage:

   1. Offer and lead magnet. The thing you dangle. Most broken channels are actually broken offers.

   2. Volume. More ads, more posts, more calls. Most "broken" channels are actually starved channels.

   3. Creative, CTAs, personalization. Make the message hit harder.

   4. Targeting. Aim it better, and once it's aimed right, stop touching it.

   5. New platforms. Last. Expand once you're crushing it, never because you couldn't make the current channel
   work.


    "Marketing always works. It's just a matter of efficiency."
    ALEX HORMOZI

THE METHOD


MORE. BETTER. NEW.
Once you've picked your method, there are only three strategies: do more of it, do it
better, or do something new. 99% of the time the answer is more or better, not new.

START WITH MORE

More is the default because more will always make you better. Reps build skill. If you're under $1M a
year, the answer is almost always more, full stop. The Rule of 100 (100 minutes or 100 actions of
marketing every day) is the primer for someone getting started. If you're trying to win, you eventually
count in thousands, not tens.


THE ACCORDION

More and better alternate like an accordion. You make one video a week, push to five, notice one of
the five outperforms, drop to three better ones, get good, expand back to ten. That oscillation is
normal and expected. It's how skill and volume grow together.


WHEN BETTER BEATS MORE

Switch to better when the incremental return on better exceeds more. With one salesperson, adding
a second doubles output and beats coaching. With twenty, moving the team's close rate from 25%
to 30% may cost less than onboarding four more reps. Strategy is prioritization of resources: same
gain, fewer resources, that's the pick.


WHEN NEW IS ALLOWED (RARELY)

   You truly maximized the market: your spend covers your marketplace many times over. Far more common
   locally than nationally.

   The platform itself is shrinking, like newspapers dropping 25% a year.

   The risk-adjusted return on new genuinely exceeds more and better, which is rare. After "more," ask "can I do
   more again?" You'd be surprised how often the answer is yes.


    "What appears to be volatility is just insufficient volume."
    ALEX HORMOZI

STAGE 01 · LEGITIMIZE


THE PLAYBOOK
1. SELL TO WARMTH FIRST

Your first customers come from people who already know you: friends, past colleagues, your
contact list, your tiny social following. This isn't a consolation prize. Warm buyers tolerate rough
edges, give honest feedback, and become your first testimonials. Tell every one of them what you
now sell and who it's for. Most won't buy. They'll refer.


2. TRADE MARGIN FOR PROOF, DELIBERATELY

Discount or even give away your service in exchange for a documented result and a review, with
the exchange agreed up front. A 10 or 20% discount changes nobody's behavior. If you discount,
make it 80 or 90%, big enough to change behavior, and attach the condition: I get your numbers,
your before-and-after, and your words.


3. CAPTURE THE STORY WHILE IT HAPPENS

Record everything you're allowed to record: sales calls, onboarding, check-ins, the moment the
result lands. You will never get this footage back, and at later stages it becomes ad inventory. Ask
for the testimonial at the moment of the win, not three months later. The question that works: "Where
were you before, and where are you now?" Let them say it in their own words.


4. PUT THE PROOF WHERE STRANGERS TRIP OVER IT

Reviews go on Google. Case studies go on your site with real numbers. Screenshots get saved to a
folder you'll use for the rest of this roadmap. If you're allowed to name the customer, name them.
Specificity is believability.


5. START THE PULSE

Post one to three times a week on the one platform your future customers use most. Not to go viral.
So that when someone checks whether you're real, there's a pulse. Sign up for the free ad credits
Google and Meta hand to new advertisers, and save them for Stage 2.


    "Do epic shit and then talk about what you did."
    ALEX HORMOZI

STAGE 02 · PUBLICIZE


THE PLAYBOOK
1. PICK ONE CHANNEL AND MARRY IT

Don't diversify in the beginning. Double down on what works. Pick by risk-adjusted return on your
existing skills: talker → outreach or video, writer → posts and email, have cash and proof → ads.
Every platform you add divides your reps. One channel, worked daily, beats four channels worked
weekly.


2. RUN THE RULE OF 100

Every day, do 100 minutes or 100 units of marketing work: 100 outreach touches, 100 minutes making
content, or managing your ad volume. The Rule of 100 is the primer for getting started. Winners
eventually count in thousands. But 100 daily, never skipped, will already put you ahead of nearly
everyone at this stage.


3. FIX THE THING YOU DANGLE

Before volume can pay, the offer at the end of it has to be worth responding to. For the love of God,
no one wants to request a quote. Build a real lead magnet, and there are only three kinds: reveal a
problem they don't know they have, give a free trial of your solution, or splinter off one step of your
full service and give it away. The heuristic: give away something other people charge for. The more
real the cost, the better it works.


4. START THE EMAIL LIST ON DAY ONE

Every lead goes onto a list, and the list gets emailed. Email is the single highest-return platform that
exists. Businesses that take it seriously drive 25 to 50% of revenue from it, and it's free. One specific
piece of value per email, then a simple call to action. If you aren't emailing your leads and
customers, you are leaving money on the table every single week.


5. IF OUTREACH OR ADS IS YOUR CHANNEL, KEEP THE PULSE

Keep posting 1 to 3 times a week where your leads check you out. That "barely alive" layer warms
every cold call and every ad click, because the first thing a serious prospect does is look you up.

THE MATH YOU MUST KNOW COLD
   MOZI MATH · BACK-OF-NAPKIN LTV

   Lifetime revenue = price ÷ monthly churn
   LTV (lifetime gross profit) = lifetime revenue × gross margin

   Months a customer stays = 1 ÷ churn
   $100/month at 10% churn is $1,000 of lifetime revenue. At 85% gross margin, that customer is
   worth $850 of gross profit. That $850 is your entire war chest for acquiring the next customer
   and running the business. Count gross profit, not revenue. Software people can use revenue
   because their margins are near-total. You probably can't.


   MOZI MATH · WILL YOU GROW OR SHRINK?

   Hypothetical max revenue = sales velocity × lifetime revenue
   Doing $1M/month, selling 20 new customers a month at $25K lifetime revenue each? Your
   ceiling is $500K/month. The business is going to shrink by half and no ad campaign will save
   it. Same $1M/month with 1,000 sales at $2K lifetime revenue is headed to $2M. Run your own
   numbers before you spend another marketing dollar.


THE ONE CAUTIONARY TALE TO MEMORIZE

Prestige Labs sold meals at $10 that cost $9 fully loaded. The team celebrated spending $10 in ads
to sell $20 of meals. But $20 of meals carried $2 of gross profit, so every $10 of ad spend destroyed
$8. That's how you make $100,000 mistakes in the blink of an eye without knowing your numbers.
ROAS without gross margin is a lie.

    to CAC."

THE PLAYBOOK
1. RAISE YOUR PRICE (YES, YOURS)

Your close rate tells you how underpriced you are. Closing 80%+ of offers? Consider tripling the
price. 60 to 80%? You're underpriced by 2 to 3x. 40 to 50%? Underpriced by 1.25 to 1.5x. Only below
30% should you fix selling before price. One gym raised $99/month to $299/month with a 14-day trial
of the upgraded service: 70% stayed at triple the price and revenue doubled. You can always
change it back.


2. BUILD THE NEXT RUNG OF THE LADDER

About 20% of your customers will buy an offer priced 5x higher, and 20% taking 5x the price doubles
the revenue of the business. The two upsells that only always work: more of the thing they just
bought, and more help with the thing they just bought. Sell the upgrade at the halfway point of
delivery, not the end. Wait until the end and you convert a third as many.


3. CUT CHURN BY CUTTING, NOT ADDING

Churn typically happens from overwhelm. People are bloodhounds for value, and diluting it across
more stuff makes them leave. Do fewer things better. Then protect the first 24 hours: quick win,
personal welcome, human touch inside 48 hours. Onboarding is a continuation of the sale.


4. SELL BETTER CUSTOMERS, NOT CHEAPER LEADS

"I need cheaper leads" is usually "I need better leads so the returns get better." 80/20 your customer
base, find where the top 20% came from, and put 5x the attention there. Add qualification friction to
your forms: budget, authority, need, timing. You may get more expensive leads and your cost per
CUSTOMER will typically go down.


5. PULL CASH FORWARD

Offer annual prepay with a discount, buy-X-get-Y-free, and prepaid future service. Cash covering
CAC is the precondition for scaling spend in Stage 4. The faster a customer's cash lands, the faster
you can buy the next customer.

delivery, not the end. Wait until the end and you convert a third as many.

THE THREE RULES OF THE MACHINE
RULE 1 — KEEP TESTING AND SCALING APART

Testing lives in campaigns where YOU control budget per ad set, so the platform can't dump all the
money on one ad before you've learned anything. Winners graduate into separate scaling
campaigns where the algorithm gets the budget. Two lanes, never mixed.


RULE 2 — TEST ONE ANGLE, ONE FORMAT AT A TIME

An angle is a different way of speaking to the customer ("your whole business depends on you" vs.
"you don't have the systems to scale"). Same person, a new door in. A format is a different way to
say the same thing (talking head, Q&A from stage, customer testimonial). Each angle-format
combo gets its own ad set with one or two ads in it, four at the absolute most. Cram in more and
the budget spreads too thin for anything to prove out.


RULE 3 — OPTIMIZE FOR THE DEEPEST ACTION IN THE FUNNEL

Most people optimize for opt-ins. Tell the platform to optimize for the action furthest down the
funnel you can feed it: booked meetings, purchases. Acquisition.com optimizes for booked
meetings, and it transformed lead quality. In one launch, purchase-optimized campaigns returned
11x while opt-in-optimized returned 4x. Same ads. Different instruction to the machine.


   MOZI MATH · THE KILL RULE

   Ad cost ≥ 3 × target cost per qualified lead → the ad is dead. Cut it.
   No feelings, no "give it the weekend." If early indicators (click-through under ~1.5%, ugly CPMs)
   are in the gutter for a couple of days, cut even sooner. Kill your losers fast and put money
   behind winners. Everyone knows this. Almost nobody does it fast enough.

THE PLAYBOOK, PART ONE: THE AD
FACTORY
1. ASSEMBLE ADS, DON'T WRITE THEM

Hooks are still 80% of the battle. Write 50+ hooks, 3 to 5 "meats" (the body of the ad), and a handful
of CTAs, then assemble the combinations. One-take versus assembled has zero effect on output
performance, and the combinatorics hand you 150 to 750 ads a week. Volume should never be your
concern again.


2. KALEIDOSCOPE YOUR WINNERS

When an ad wins, make 100 permutations of it: different opener, spokesperson, background,
clothing, font, speed at 1.2x and 0.9x. One winning gym ad made roughly $10M, and it wasn't one ad.
It was a hundred versions of that ad. Don't hunt new angles while a winner still has juice; change the
packaging.


3. DOCUMENT THE PROCESS, THEN HAND IT TO AGENTS

The meta-rule from the team that does this daily: humans did work, we documented the work, and
then we gave it to AI. Write your editor's process click by click, one layer more detailed than feels
necessary. Turn the SOPs into agent skill files. Correct mistakes once and bake the correction in. The
editor who documented 1,000 manual edits now ships a year's worth in a week, and the agent never
forgets and never takes vacations.


4. MINE YOUR ASSETS

Everything the business has produced is training data: your best emails, your top sales call
transcripts, winning ads, testimonials, FAQs. AI sounds like a melting pot of the internet until you train
it on your body of work. Then it sounds like you. Expect amplification, not automation: 4x to 8x
leverage per asset type is the realistic, measured range. The idea is still the alpha, and the ideas still
come from you.

THE PLAYBOOK
1. DOCUMENT ASPIRATIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS

Land Rover shows trucks conquering mountains so a parent believes it'll handle two inches of snow.
Arc'teryx outfits Everest climbers so a commuter trusts it car-to-door. The formula: achieve things
orders of magnitude beyond your avatar's aspirations, then document them relentlessly. Your
customer reverse-engineers the believability on their own. Do epic things, then talk about what you
did.


2. GIVE AWAY THE SECRETS, SELL THE IMPLEMENTATION

At scale, free value is the trust engine. Give it all away. No one's going to do it anyway; everyone's
busy, and the few who do it themselves become your loudest advocates. Goodwill at industrial
volume is what "brand" is made of, and copycats are a signal you matter. Be afraid of the day they
stop copying you.


3. SAY ONE CLEAR THING, EVERYWHERE, FOREVER

A brand is a promise repeated until strangers can recite it. One clear message about who you are
and who you're for, kept stable while creative varies around it. Associate with brands and people
your avatar already trusts and let their trust transfer.


4. RUN A PORTFOLIO, MEASURE IT HOLISTICALLY

Multiple channels now behave like one system, so measure them like one system. Attribution lags
execution by about a year; the best you'll get is directional data plus first principles, and waiting for
perfect data makes you too slow. Judge the mix by blended CAC, LTV:CAC, and demand you didn't
pay for this quarter: branded search, direct traffic, "heard about you from" answers.


5. GO WHERE THE AFFINITY IS DEEPEST

The closest approximation to being there in person wins the most loyalty: long form beats shorts for
depth, live beats recorded, interactive beats broadcast. Shorts get you discovered. Longs and lives
get you believed.

       passive income beats your paycheck."
